scenes.tts: Chapter one showed a motor walking by gripping, swinging, releasing, and resetting. But how can experiments reveal the direction, steps, and pull of a machine too small to resolve?
scenes.caption: Chapter 1 showed a motor walking by gripping, swinging, releasing, and resetting. But how can experiments reveal the direction, steps, and pull of a machine too small to resolve?
scenes.visual: Continue chapter 1's world without a cut: a large orange kinesin carries a yellow cargo rightward on the same blue tiled microtubule. Add a small persistent label 'schematic' at lower right. The GRIP, SWING, LET GO, RE-COCK dial turns in the corner. On 'too small to resolve', the camera pulls back until the motor becomes a single orange point inside a large microscope field. A question mark grows around that point while the microtubule continues shimmering.
scenes.narration: Chapter 1 showed a motor walking by gripping, swinging, releasing, and resetting. But how can experiments reveal the direction, steps, and pull of a machine too small to resolve?

scenes.visual: Title card over the carried microscope field, at most 2 seconds: lesson name 'Molecular Motors and Cargo' and film title 'Turning Motion Into a Measurement'. The orange point and blue track remain faintly visible and moving behind the words; retain the small 'schematic' label.

scenes.tts: Begin with a gliding assay. Purified motors are fastened by their tails to a glass coverslip. Add fluorescent tracks and A T P. The motors cannot travel, but their feet can still walk. A fluorescence microscope follows the long glowing tracks; each motor is far too small to resolve.
scenes.caption: Begin with a gliding assay. Purified motors are fastened by their tails to a glass coverslip. Add fluorescent tracks and ATP. The motors cannot travel, but their feet can still walk. A fluorescence microscope follows the long glowing tracks; each motor is far too small to resolve.
scenes.visual: The microscope field transforms into a side view of one grey glass coverslip filling the lower third; retain the small 'schematic' label. Four large orange motor cartoons descend tail-first and lock to the glass with small clamps; their feet face upward. A long plain blue track (no chevrons, no end marks, so nothing shows which end is plus) slides in above them, filling most of the frame width. Green ATP chips drift in continuously. Each orange foot cycles through grip, swing, let go and re-cock while its tail remains visibly clamped.
scenes.narration: Begin with a gliding assay. Purified motors are fastened by their tails to a glass coverslip. Add fluorescent tracks and ATP. The motors cannot travel, but their feet can still walk. A fluorescence microscope follows the long glowing tracks; each motor is far too small to resolve.

scenes.tts: Imagine a free motor that walks right on a fixed track. Clamp that motor instead, and every stroke pushes the loose track left. The same interaction now moves the other partner. It resembles walking on a loose rug while bolted in place.
scenes.caption: Imagine a free motor that walks right on a fixed track. Clamp that motor instead, and every stroke pushes the loose track left. The same interaction now moves the other partner. It resembles walking on a loose rug while bolted in place.
scenes.visual: Split the carried setup into two stacked schematic views, labelled 'schematic' at lower right. Top: one orange motor walks right along a fixed plain blue bar (no chevrons or plus/minus marks), with a short white arrow labelled 'free motor'. Bottom: the same motor shape is clamped to glass; its foot strokes right while the blue bar glides left. A dotted vertical guide shows that the track, not the clamp, changes position. Both motions loop slowly through the scene.
scenes.narration: Imagine a free motor that walks right on a fixed track. Clamp that motor instead, and every stroke pushes the loose track left. The same interaction now moves the other partner. It resembles walking on a loose rug while bolted in place.

scenes.tts: Mark the track's two ends, then watch which end leads. Because the track glides opposite the motor's walk, that movie reveals direction. It also reports speed across many motors at once.
scenes.caption: Mark the track's two ends, then watch which end leads. Because the track glides opposite the motor's walk, that movie reveals direction. It also reports speed across many motors at once.
scenes.visual: Return to the single gliding chamber, retaining the small 'schematic' label. The blue track gains a large circle on its left end and a triangle on its right, with no plus or minus labels. As it glides left, the circle leads and a camera frame follows it. A white ruler beneath the chamber and a timer in the corner advance together; a computed position-versus-time line grows steadily in a small inset labelled 'many motors'.
scenes.narration: Mark the track's two ends, then watch which end leads. Because the track glides opposite the motor's walk, that movie reveals direction. It also reports speed across many motors at once.

scenes.tts: To see one motor, reverse the geometry again. Fix the blue track. Attach one motor to a yellow bead, then place that bead inside a focused laser trap. Sparse coating makes most beads carry at most one motor, separating one walker from the crowd.
scenes.caption: To see one motor, reverse the geometry again. Fix the blue track. Attach one motor to a yellow bead, then place that bead inside a focused laser trap. Sparse coating makes most beads carry at most one motor, separating one walker from the crowd.
scenes.visual: The grey coverslip and fixed motors rotate away; retain the small 'schematic' label. The same blue track settles onto two clamps and becomes fixed. The four orange motors merge into one orange motor, which attaches to a large yellow bead. A broad white laser cone appears above the bead and narrows to a glowing ring labelled 'trap centre'. The motor begins walking right and the bead follows.
scenes.narration: To see one motor, reverse the geometry again. Fix the blue track. Attach one motor to a yellow bead, then place that bead inside a focused laser trap. Sparse coating makes most beads carry at most one motor, separating one walker from the crowd.

scenes.tts: Suppose the motor advances in equal jumps, with waits between them. What shape should the bead's position record make? Pause and predict.
scenes.caption: Suppose the motor advances in equal jumps, with waits between them. What shape should the bead's position record make? Pause and predict.
scenes.visual: The schematic walking motor freezes just after landing while the bead continues a gentle trap-centred wobble; keep 'schematic' at lower right. A large empty graph fills the upper half, axes labelled 'time' and 'bead position'. A question card asks 'smooth ramp or staircase?' A moving dot waits at the graph origin.
scenes.narration: Suppose the motor advances in equal jumps, with waits between them. What shape should the bead's position record make? Pause and predict.

scenes.visual: Thinking pause. Keep 'smooth ramp or staircase?', the 'schematic' label and the empty axes on screen. The trapped bead wobbles gently, the blue track shimmers, and the graph's origin dot pulses once; reveal no answer.

scenes.tts: A staircase. Flat stretches are waits; sudden rises are steps. Kinesin bead records showed rises eight nanometres high. Timing the flat stretches shows how long the motor waits before each jump. The invisible walk became a measured step size and a step rate.
scenes.caption: A staircase. Flat stretches are waits; sudden rises are steps. Kinesin bead records showed rises 8 nanometres high. Timing the flat stretches shows how long the motor waits before each jump. The invisible walk became a measured step size and a step rate.
scenes.visual: The graph draws a computed staircase as the schematic orange motor takes four visible steps; keep 'schematic' beside the cartoon, not the computed graph. Flat stretches have unequal, randomly varying lengths. During each wait the trace stays flat while the bead wobbles; at each landing it rises. A vertical bracket on one rise reads '8 nm'. A counter below advances 'step 1, 2, 3, 4' and a timer runs, then both combine into a badge labelled 'steps per second'.
scenes.narration: A staircase. Flat stretches are waits; sudden rises are steps. Kinesin bead records showed rises 8 nanometres high. Timing the flat stretches shows how long the motor waits before each jump. The invisible walk became a measured step size and a step rate.

scenes.tts: The trap also behaves like a spring. Pull the bead from the centre, and the restoring force grows. After calibration, displacement becomes force. Trap stiffness says how much force each nanometre of displacement adds. Farther from centre means a larger opposing load.
scenes.caption: The trap also behaves like a spring. Pull the bead from the centre, and the restoring force grows. After calibration, displacement becomes force. Trap stiffness says how much force each nanometre of displacement adds. Farther from centre means a larger opposing load.
scenes.visual: Clear the graph but keep the same schematic bead, motor and track, labelled 'schematic'. A red elastic arrow connects the yellow bead to the glowing trap centre. With each motor step, the bead moves farther right and the red arrow lengthens and thickens. A red force gauge is computed from displacement using a fixed stiffness; its scale is labelled 'calibrated'. The motor's steps visibly slow as the opposing arrow grows.
scenes.narration: The trap also behaves like a spring. Pull the bead from the centre, and the restoring force grows. After calibration, displacement becomes force. Trap stiffness says how much force each nanometre of displacement adds. Farther from centre means a larger opposing load.

scenes.tts: Eventually the motor may stall: it keeps trying, but makes no net progress. The bead's offset then reports the opposing force. Different loads reveal how the motor's speed changes as resistance grows. Position, time, and calibration turn motion into steps, speed, and pull.
scenes.caption: Eventually the motor may stall: it keeps trying, but makes no net progress. The bead's offset then reports the opposing force. Different loads reveal how the motor's speed changes as resistance grows. Position, time, and calibration turn motion into steps, speed, and pull.
scenes.visual: The schematic orange feet continue small cycling motions, but the motor and bead stop advancing; keep the 'schematic' label. A bracket from trap centre to bead settles at a fixed length and the computed red gauge holds. Three readouts transform from the carried objects: staircase height becomes 'step', graph slope becomes 'speed', and the calibrated red gauge becomes 'force'. Each readout stays connected by a thin line to the measurement that produced it.
scenes.narration: Eventually the motor may stall: it keeps trying, but makes no net progress. The bead's offset then reports the opposing force. Different loads reveal how the motor's speed changes as resistance grows. Position, time, and calibration turn motion into steps, speed, and pull.

scenes.tts: But a number belongs to its setup. In a fixed trap, load rises as the bead moves. Feedback can hold load constant instead. Compare motors only under matched fuel and loading conditions. Otherwise, a neat calculation can combine measurements that never occurred together.
scenes.caption: But a number belongs to its setup. In a fixed trap, load rises as the bead moves. Feedback can hold load constant instead. Compare motors only under matched fuel and loading conditions. Otherwise, a neat calculation can combine measurements that never occurred together.
scenes.visual: Split the schematic trap view and retain its label. Top, labelled 'fixed trap': the centre stays put, bead displacement and the computed red load gauge rise together. Bottom, labelled 'constant load': the trap centre slides right by feedback, keeping the red arrow and gauge constant while the motor advances. A green ATP gauge appears beside both. A comparison bracket between the panels stays grey while the loading methods and ATP gauges differ; then the bottom panel switches to 'fixed trap' with the same ATP level, and only then does the bracket turn white.
scenes.narration: But a number belongs to its setup. In a fixed trap, load rises as the bead moves. Feedback can hold load constant instead. Compare motors only under matched fuel and loading conditions. Otherwise, a neat calculation can combine measurements that never occurred together.

scenes.tts: One bench, two choices. Fix the motor, and the track reports direction. Hold the bead, and its motion reports steps and force. Change what is held still, and motion becomes a measurement.
scenes.caption: One bench, two choices. Fix the motor, and the track reports direction. Hold the bead, and its motion reports steps and force. Change what is held still, and motion becomes a measurement.
scenes.visual: The frame reunites into one schematic microscope bench, labelled 'schematic'. Left, orange motors clamped to grey glass drive the marked blue track left. Right, one orange motor on a fixed blue track pulls the yellow trapped bead right while a computed staircase and red force gauge update. A white clamp icon moves from motor to track to bead on the three clauses. On the final sentence, the two views fold into one large moving arrow passing through a ruler and emerging as a clean measurement tick.
scenes.narration: One bench, two choices. Fix the motor, and the track reports direction. Hold the bead, and its motion reports steps and force. Change what is held still, and motion becomes a measurement.

scenes.visual: End card line: 'Hold one thing still, and motion becomes a measurement.' Behind it, faint but moving and labelled 'schematic', the marked blue track glides on the left and the yellow bead traces computed steps on the right.
